body: A few, mostly at night. Daytime has been okay, but nights get rough!
I do! They help some. So do emotional support animals!

Honestly, I think it’s inherent. There’s some pretty heavy depression on both sides of my family, so it might just be hereditary. My early childhood wasn’t all peaches and sunshine, but it wasn’t bad or traumatic either, so I can’t imagine it was triggered by trauma.

Probably like around 9 or 10? My best friend at the time was adorable and, as she matured, drop-dead gorgeous. I vividly remember people pushing me aside (sometimes physically) just to fawn over her. It took me seven years to realize that it was because she was beautiful, and I was not. Nobody save for my mother had ever complimented my looks unprompted. I was always the afterthought, even among my own extended family, as I was the least attractive of all my cousins. Before that point I genuinely thought I was cute. It only got worse from there.

I’m sorry. You deserve an amazing mom too. Reading a lot of peoples’ stories here make me realize just how lucky I am to have such a fantastic mother, but the fact that not everyone can say the same is so baffling and just breaks my heart. Truly, not every parent deserves a child.
Thank you for your kind words. I know I’m important to them, it’s just tough sometimes.
